text:
Ivan Provorov came back on Oct 31, and Columbus noticed. The Blue Jackets beat Colorado 7-2 in his second game back, with Provorov scoring, and Zach Werenski talked to The Hockey Writers about the impact of having him out and then back in a full lineup.

Four games is too small a sample to say much, but the early signs are good: Columbus has had 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, almost ten points better than without him, and he played nearly 26 minutes in a 2-1 win over Dallas.

Last season is the better guide. Evolving-Hockey had him 41st among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense, and he played all 82 games with 31 points. He's 29, the seventh pick in 2015, taken one spot ahead of Werenski. Our projection sees about 24 points from here. We'd watch his ice time; that's where Columbus will show how much it needs him.
